eligibility.quote: This problem seems to be related to Fast-RTPS. Using OpenSplice for DDS implementation, I can't reproduce this problem unlike Fast-RTPS.

notes: Issue #755 ("Listener stops working") documents a stall in message delivery at high publish rates. I read the issue body (listener "**STOPS** after receiving some messages (random amount)") and the thread: jacobperron ("It sounds like a bug."), ivanpauno ("I have been able to reproduce it on Linux (after retrying a bunch of times). The worst case I have seen: our demos with the timer changed to 100us, published up to message number 4700, listened up to message 4676."), vinnamkim (the quote above), and clalancette ("you are using a 'reliable' QoS ... all of the messages must be acknowledged before they are dropped from the queue ... try switching to 'Best Effort'"). I also read Fast-DDS#571, where the failure reproduces with Fast-RTPS's native API (no ROS code) and eProsima's lauramg15 attributes it to the writer settings: "This problem can be solved reducing the heartbeat period." The stall therefore lives inside the middleware's reliable transport and occurs with any correct publisher/subscriber pair; it does not depend on an assumption between the two ROS nodes. E2 stops at step 2 (internal), which is correct. Loudness/resolution correctly null.
